Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.
Then h is classically pluriharmonic and locally R-PL. If X is pure-dimensional, then h is also
GJR harmonic.
Corollary 5.2. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that h is not classically pluriharmonic. For every analytic extension L/K, at least one of the
following failures occurs:

                                                 42

 (1) d0 d00 [hL ] 6= 0;

 (2) one of hL and −hL has nonnegative Hessian current but does not belong to the CLD-psh
     hierarchy.

For L = K, the ﬁrst alternative is impossible. Hence every negative answer to P06.2 furnishes,
in one of the two signs of h, a continuous zero-current function outside the CLD-psh hierarchy.
If X is pure-dimensional, this is a counterexample to the converse of Book Proposition 15.9.8
in its stated scope.

    This reduction neither pulls a continuous current through an arbitrary scalar extension
nor proves positive-current regularization. It identiﬁes those operations as distinct proof
obligations and shows that a negative answer to P06.2 produces a zero-current function outside
the CLD-psh hierarchy at the ground ﬁeld. In the pure-dimensional scope this would disprove
the missing nonsmooth converse in Book Proposition 15.9.8.

GJR harmonic. This does not supply locally twisted annular coordinates at the top or insert
annular stages at arbitrary intermediate levels of the tower.
     Annular geometry may also occur at the bottom. The general transfer statement Book
Proposition M.1.34 isolates the common exact descent, classical-pluriharmonic transfer, R-
harmonic transfer, and ﬁrst-current-rigidity transfer of the four allowed bundle types over an
arbitrary admissible base. Applying it to a globally coordinated curve-polyannulus product
gives Book Corollary M.1.53: after any such mixed tower, the top function still has the
unique logarithmic coeﬃcient formula over the original curve. Applying it instead to a locally
trivial curve-polyannulus bundle or a locally trivial mixed curve-polycylinder bundle gives
Book Corollary M.1.54, Book Corollary M.1.55, with classical pluriharmonicity, local R-PL
regularity, and GJR harmonicity but no global coeﬃcient formula. Thus locally twisted
annular coordinates are now allowed at the bottom of the mixed exact tower. The result
still requires their displayed analytic local trivializations and does not allow an annular stage
to be interleaved at an arbitrary later level, an annular ﬁbration without such charts, or an
arbitrary nonproduct germ.
     For globally coordinated annular products, the two endpoint orders can be fully interleaved.
In Book Theorem M.1.20, each stage of a ﬁnite boundaryless tower over the curve may be
either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

                                               56

     For the three regularity conclusions, part of that monodromy obstruction can be removed.
In Book Corollary M.1.33, one analytic open cover of the original curve is allowed to coordinate
every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.
Thus curve-controlled locally twisted annular stages may occur at arbitrary levels. The result
deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not
retain the preceding tower or its paracompactness hypotheses.
     There is also a nonproduct endpoint-base range. If the base is a positive- dimensional
standard strict endpoint polycylinder and the ﬁbre is a locally trivial standard strict open
polydisc, then Book Proposition M.1.37 pulls every full zero-current function back from the
explicit aﬃne combination of the base annular logarithms. Thus it is classically pluriharmonic,
locally R-PL, and GJR harmonic. This allows open, closed, and half-closed annuli in the base,
but still does not treat an annular ﬁbre, a ﬁbration without the displayed local product charts,
or an equation only on a strict radial core. The same formula persists through every ﬁnite
tower of the displayed locally trivial strict open-polydisc bundles: Book Corollary M.1.56
ﬁrst descends the function to the endpoint-polycylinder base and then applies the endpoint
classiﬁcation. Each level must carry the stated local product charts; the nontrivial tower
result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.
     There is a further invariant nonproduct range. Let the base be a good, topologically sepa-
rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-
clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the
completion of an algebraic extension when the base becomes the displayed split toric domain
and all three of the lifted action, invariance, and zero-current conditions hold upstairs; see
Book Corollary M.1.68. The corresponding ﬁnite-tower statement is Book Corollary M.1.69;
it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book
Corollary M.1.71 requires a complete displayed tower near each point of the total space, with
the scalar-stable extension, the compatible action on every level, and equivariance of every
map. It supplies the same three conclusions locally, but does not create that tower or transfer
a downstairs current equation upstairs.
     The former third atom in this environment is now resolved. Book Theorem 19.3.4 proves
that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an
algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ﬁeld is, locally on a strict aﬃnoid neigh-
bourhood, a uniformly convergent decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh func-
tions. Equivalently, current positivity, Thuillier subharmonicity, and the ﬁrst ordinary-smooth

decreasing-limit stage coincide in this scope. The proof passes through ﬁnite local tree skeleta,

task.problem:
Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary

result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.
     There is a further invariant nonproduct range. Let the base be a good, topologically sepa-
rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-
clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the
completion of an algebraic extension when the base becomes the displayed split toric domain
and all three of the lifted action, invariance, and zero-current conditions hold upstairs; see
Book Corollary M.1.68. The corresponding ﬁnite-tower statement is Book Corollary M.1.69;
it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book
Corollary M.1.71 requires a complete displayed tower near each point of the total space, with
the scalar-stable extension, the compatible action on every level, and equivariance of every
map. It supplies the same three conclusions locally, but does not create that tower or transfer
a downstairs current equation upstairs.

that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an
algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ﬁeld is, locally on a strict aﬃnoid neigh-
bourhood, a uniformly convergent decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh func-
tions. Equivalently, current positivity, Thuillier subharmonicity, and the ﬁrst ordinary-smooth

curve which is not even a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD-smooth harmonic functions.

the now-proved psh regularization theorem, whose approximants carry positive curvature

notes.text:
Claim R16. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued; X good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure one-dimensional; U any ordinary open; and h:U→R finite continuous with D[h]=0 for ordinary analytic CLD currents, D=d'd''. With C=completion(algebraic closure K), every x∈U_C has a compact strict affinoid Y inside any prescribed ordinary neighborhood, with x in its actual ordinary interior, and sequences u_n^±∈C(Y) decreasing on all Y and uniformly converging to ±h_C. Each approximant is ordinary CLD-smooth and psh on that same actual interior. Y is fixed before n and either sign. Actual nilpotent calibration is retained.

The complete authoritative argument is P06.2-argument.md. It directly reproduces the operative T2–T13, C1–C4 and B dependency arguments and their exact primary source statements/proof bodies. No predecessor acceptance is a premise. T reconstructs finite separable differentiated scalar-test approximation, real averaging in wild cases, inseparable Frobenius descent, embedded mixed stages and exact compact finite-stage test descent at completion. Its calibrated estimates control carrier total variation before pushforward, including curve segments lying entirely in Newton collision walls. CLD15.3.1 then supplies actual top-measure projection with no scalar degree factor. Local purity and the original ambient hypotheses are checked. B proves algebraic closedness of the completed algebraic closure by compatible roots of rapidly converging monic polynomial approximants.

C separates reduced components with their own positive generic lengths, removes continuous rigid punctures using shrinking cutoffs of bounded calibrated variation, and transports the equation through normalization on its actual isomorphism locus. Over C the normalization is smooth. Van der Put1.1 applies to connected normal strict affinoids over this complete algebraically closed field; boundary composition identifies actual ordinary interiors with ordinary opens in smooth proper algebraic curves. Wanner1801.04713v3 Theorem4.7 applies there to both signs. Her algebraic tests are ordinary analytic tests; no reverse test-class equality is needed. Two-sign Dirichlet comparison gives Thuillier harmonicity on the normalization.

New construction at rigid points: harmonicity on strict disc neighborhoods with singleton Shilov boundary forces constancy by Thuillier2.3.9. Unit-norm rigidity gives the same ordinary-neighborhood conclusion. The normalization has finitely many rigid preimages. Removing the closed image of the compact complement of their constant neighborhoods gives an actual constant ordinary neighborhood downstairs, including nilpotents. Constant sequences σh(a)+4^-n suffice.

At a nonrigid point, remove the locally finite rigid conductor/intersection set. The reduction is one smooth branch. The full semistable disc/annulus/star structure gives an ordinary star inside any prescribed open; compactness requires truncating only finitely many exceptional directions. Choose an actual strict affinoid Y inside it. Its reduced finite skeleton lies in a tree and therefore has no circuit. Harmonic/lisse refinement gives h=F∘τ on one fixed finite tree Γ, with F edgewise affine and zero interior graph Laplacian. The same Y and Γ handle both signs.

For ε>0, root Γ at a boundary vertex. Assign μ=1 to interior vertices, μ=0 to other boundary vertices, and μ(root)=−number of interior vertices. Integer edge slopes given by subtree sums yield Δψ=μ. Add a sufficiently small δψ to σF, then approximate finitely many edge slopes independently by rationals. A tree permits integration without period conditions. With total length L and maximal valency d, the additional uniform error is at most Lη and the Laplacian error at most dη. Thus G is uniformly close and has strictly positive interior vertex masses.

At an interior type-2 vertex z, the rational residual graph divisor B has positive degree. Choose N clearing denominators with deg(NB)≥2g+1. Serre duality gives H¹(O(NB)(−p))=0 for every residual point p. Evaluation is surjective, and over the infinite algebraically closed residue field a section avoids every finitely forbidden graph/exceptional direction. Its effective zero divisor A satisfies A∼NB and has fresh support. Hence B−A/N is a rational multiple of a principal divisor. Thuillier2.3.22’s slope sequences, with residual-function lifting reconstructed using density of the analytic residue field and the annular order formula, give one ordinary unit-log harmonic germ H_z: prescribed graph slopes, fresh slopes −a_p, zero remaining slopes, and value G(z). One finite unit tuple and common lisse refinement provide exact equality on whole ordinary overlaps.

Use the ordinary annular coordinate t=−log|T|+c in each fresh direction. An even smooth mollifier defines m_η(s,t)=(s+t+(|·|*ρ_η)(s−t))/2. This is smooth, convex, nondecreasing, agrees with max outside |s−t|<η, and differs from max by at most η/2. Replace G(z)−at by m_η(G(z)−at,G(z)−ar), choosing η<ar and ar+η/2<ε within a sufficiently short collar. It equals H_z near z and its constant continuation farther down the whole disc. It carries positive curvature and does not return to the old constant. Type-3 positive kinks are smoothed similarly. Finitely many disjoint collars and equality on actual ordinary open overlaps glue a continuous g on Y, ordinary smooth/psh on its interior, with arbitrarily small uniform error. Only scalar tests are partitioned when verifying positivity; psh functions are not glued by partitions.

Nilpotents remain actual. Lift local finite unit tuples through the quotient defining the reduction; their numerical logarithmic norms agree. Scalar-section nullity supplies the same ordinary smooth numerical function on Y. Every actual nonnegative compact ordinary test ψ restricts to a nonnegative reduced test ψ₀, and D commutes with restriction. CLD16.6.3 gives D[g]_Y(ψ)=ℓ∫gDψ₀≥0, where ℓ is the actual positive generic Artinian length. Constant rigid neighborhoods use the corresponding sum over component lengths. No length-one replacement or higher-form sheaf identification is assumed.

Choose g_n^σ with error<b_n=4^-n on this fixed Y and set c_n=Σ_{j≥n}(b_j+b_{j+1})=(5/3)b_n, u_n^σ=g_n^σ+c_n. Then c_n−c_{n+1}=b_n+b_{n+1}, proving monotonicity everywhere on Y, and the uniform error is below (8/3)b_n. Both signs use the common fixed neighborhood.

This also proves Bridge H16: over an algebraically closed field, a continuous function harmonic on the smooth normalization of its reduction has zero ordinary Hessian current. Uniform approximation pairs against every actual compact test with error bounded by the uniform error times the finite variation of its calibrated smooth Hessian measure. Both opposite currents are nonnegative; compact nonnegative cutoff decomposition extends their vanishing to every ordinary scalar test.

notes.text:
Theorem E16 claims: under n1’s ground-field hypotheses, every complete analytic extension L/K satisfies D[h_L]=0 on the actual U_L for the full ordinary analytic CLD test class. This is an unverified pure-curve proof draft, not arbitrary-dimensional ascent or ordinary-smooth approximation on U_L itself.

Put F=completion(algebraic closure L). Extend the K-embedding of algebraic closure K into an algebraic closure of L by adjoining roots. Uniqueness of the finite extending absolute value makes the embedding isometric on finite K-subfields; completion gives C→F. B’s compatible-root argument proves F algebraically closed. F/C need not be algebraic.

By n1’s reconstructed transport and recognition, locally over C the finite normalization N of the reduction maps surjectively to U_C, is smooth strict boundaryless, and the lifted function is Thuillier harmonic. Base change gives a finite surjective smooth pure-curve cover N_F→U_F. Outside the original locally finite rigid conductor/intersection set it remains an actual isomorphism after reduction. The excluded strict zero-dimensional algebras become finite Artinian F-algebras, so their support remains locally finite and rigid. The original reduction kernel remains nilpotent. Away from that support the actual U_F is a nilpotent thickening of a smooth branch.

Thuillier Proposition2.3.18 preserves the harmonic sheaf on a smooth strict curve under every non-Archimedean extension. Its proof uses Lemma2.3.5: the semistable skeletal scalar map is a surjective G-local isomorphism of weighted integral polyhedra, and boundary support of the graph Laplacian is equivalent before and after extension. Definitions2.3.12–2.3.16 give the sheaf assertion. These complete bodies are embedded in the main manuscript. This transports an already harmonic function, not a current. At excluded rigid points, all finitely many preimages have constant ordinary neighborhoods; finite compact quotient shrinking gives constancy downstairs. At nonrigid points, n1’s ordinary finite-tree/fresh-cap construction and actual nilpotent test argument apply. Bridge H16 therefore gives D[h_F]=0 against every ordinary analytic scalar test. No current equation after F/C was assumed, and Wanner’s test class is not used in reverse.

Geometry is checked separately. Finite surjectivity from N_F makes U_F locally pure one-dimensional: integral finite component images retain their dimensions, and every target minimal component has a source component above it. Scalar affinoid total dimension on U_L is at most one by CLD11.2.3. A point of local dimension zero would have a zero-dimensional affinoid neighborhood after removal of all one-dimensional components. Its scalar extension to F would be nonempty and still zero-dimensional, contradicting purity of U_F. Affinoid presentations, diagonal base change and GR2.11(5′) retain goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness. Actual nilpotents retain their calibration.

Every compact ordinary smooth scalar test ψ on U_L pulls back compactly to U_F: cover its support by finitely many ordinary affinoid interiors and use their compact scalar affinoids. Smooth D commutes with pullback. CLD15.3.1 states that the pushforward of a scalar-pulled locally integrable calibrated (n,n)-form measure equals its original measure. Its embedded proof uses CLD14.3.6 and actual Artinian degree sums, including nilpotents and inseparable degrees. There is no scalar degree factor. Consequently

∫_{U_L}h_L(Dψ)_Rad = ∫_{U_F}h_F(Dπ*ψ)_Rad = 0.

The continuous multiplier is bounded on the compact support. Since ψ was arbitrary, this proves the full ordinary-current equation by measure pairings, not by defining pullback of arbitrary continuous currents.

The complete proof is Theorem E16 in P06.2-argument.md, also in P06.2-partial.tex and P06.2-partial.pdf. Rerun python3 prepare.py and python3 build-and-check.py. This uses n1’s harmonic recognition and ordinary bridge. Original arbitrary-dimensional P06.2 and P05.2 remain open; independent review is required.

task.problem:
Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for
every zero-current function. The gauges are not asserted to be logarithms of analytic units,
so this criterion does not manufacture global annular coordinates. Even when the full class
does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar
contraction with the radiance class vanishes. Its exact sequence also shows that an injective
contraction, and in particular the absence of parallel dual sections, forces unique descent of
every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen
aﬃne gauge splits this sequence.

                                               56

     For the three regularity conclusions, part of that monodromy obstruction can be removed.
In Book Corollary M.1.33, one analytic open cover of the original curve is allowed to coordinate
every annular stage after base change. On each member of the cover, the whole restricted
tower is an instance of the interleaved theorem; the local conclusions therefore glue even
though the annular coordinates, radii, and product trivializations need not agree on overlaps.
Thus curve-controlled locally twisted annular stages may occur at arbitrary levels. The result
deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations
available only over arbitrary opens of intermediate tower levels, because such opens need not
retain the preceding tower or its paracompactness hypotheses.
     There is also a nonproduct endpoint-base range. If the base is a positive- dimensional
standard strict endpoint polycylinder and the ﬁbre is a locally trivial standard strict open
polydisc, then Book Proposition M.1.37 pulls every full zero-current function back from the
explicit aﬃne combination of the base annular logarithms. Thus it is classically pluriharmonic,
locally R-PL, and GJR harmonic. This allows open, closed, and half-closed annuli in the base,
but still does not treat an annular ﬁbre, a ﬁbration without the displayed local product charts,
or an equation only on a strict radial core. The same formula persists through every ﬁnite
tower of the displayed locally trivial strict open-polydisc bundles: Book Corollary M.1.56
ﬁrst descends the function to the endpoint-polycylinder base and then applies the endpoint
classiﬁcation. Each level must carry the stated local product charts; the nontrivial tower
result retains the formula together with local R-PL and GJR harmonicity, by propagating its
local curve-product charts. This still does not cover annular ﬁbres or ﬁbrations without them.
     There is a further invariant nonproduct range. Let the base be a good, topologically sepa-
rated, strict, pure positive-dimensional open inverse image in the extended tropicalization of
a split toric variety, and let a locally trivial standard strict open-polydisc bundle carry a lift
of its maximal compact torus action. If the continuous zero-current function is invariant for
that lifted action, then Book Corollary M.1.63 ﬁrst descends it to an invariant zero-current
function on the toric base and then applies the split-toric boundary theorem. It is therefore
locally real-PL, Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ harmonic, and classically pluriharmonic. The action,
invariance, and actual local open-polydisc trivializations are hypotheses: this supplies no con-
clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the
completion of an algebraic extension when the base becomes the displayed split toric domain
and all three of the lifted action, invariance, and zero-current conditions hold upstairs; see
Book Corollary M.1.68. The corresponding ﬁnite-tower statement is Book Corollary M.1.69;
it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book
Corollary M.1.71 requires a complete displayed tower near each point of the total space, with
the scalar-stable extension, the compatible action on every level, and equivariance of every
map. It supplies the same three conclusions locally, but does not create that tower or transfer
a downstairs current equation upstairs.
     The former third atom in this environment is now resolved. Book Theorem 19.3.4 proves
that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an
algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ﬁeld is, locally on a strict aﬃnoid neigh-
bourhood, a uniformly convergent decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh func-
tions. Equivalently, current positivity, Thuillier subharmonicity, and the ﬁrst ordinary-smooth

decreasing-limit stage coincide in this scope. The proof passes through ﬁnite local tree skeleta,
rational strictiﬁcation of graph Laplacians, Riemann–Roch movement of residual divisors into
fresh disc directions, and smooth convex caps. The exact frozen statement and proof passed
production Rethlas run 20260827T090645Z_767cbf81c723, using gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh,
with ﬁnal verdict correct, zero critical errors, and zero gaps. The direct endpoint did not
assign an item identiﬁer.
    The formerly written harmonic-approximant strengthening is false: Book Proposi-
tion 19.3.2 constructs an integral PL weakly smooth harmonic function on a smooth proper
curve which is not even a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD-smooth harmonic functions.
Its ﬁxed-support argument uses zero curvature of every approximant and says nothing against
the now-proved psh regularization theorem, whose approximants carry positive curvature
in fresh directions. The exact-live proposition and proof passed production Rethlas run

Claim R16. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued; X good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure one-dimensional; U any ordinary open; and h:U→R finite continuous with D[h]=0 for ordinary analytic CLD currents, D=d'd''. With C=completion(algebraic closure K), every x∈U_C has a compact strict affinoid Y inside any prescribed ordinary neighborhood, with x in its actual ordinary interior, and sequences u_n^±∈C(Y) decreasing on all Y and uniformly converging to ±h_C. Each approximant is ordinary CLD-smooth and psh on that same actual interior. Y is fixed before n and either sign. Actual nilpotent calibration is retained.

The complete authoritative argument is P06.2-argument.md. It directly reproduces the operative T2–T13, C1–C4 and B dependency arguments and their exact primary source statements/proof bodies. No predecessor acceptance is a premise. T reconstructs finite separable differentiated scalar-test approximation, real averaging in wild cases, inseparable Frobenius descent, embedded mixed stages and exact compact finite-stage test descent at completion. Its calibrated estimates control carrier total variation before pushforward, including curve segments lying entirely in Newton collision walls. CLD15.3.1 then supplies actual top-measure projection with no scalar degree factor. Local purity and the original ambient hypotheses are checked. B proves algebraic closedness of the completed algebraic closure by compatible roots of rapidly converging monic polynomial approximants.

C separates reduced components with their own positive generic lengths, removes continuous rigid punctures using shrinking cutoffs of bounded calibrated variation, and transports the equation through normalization on its actual isomorphism locus. Over C the normalization is smooth. Van der Put1.1 applies to connected normal strict affinoids over this complete algebraically closed field; boundary composition identifies actual ordinary interiors with ordinary opens in smooth proper algebraic curves. Wanner1801.04713v3 Theorem4.7 applies there to both signs. Her algebraic tests are ordinary analytic tests; no reverse test-class equality is needed. Two-sign Dirichlet comparison gives Thuillier harmonicity on the normalization.

New construction at rigid points: harmonicity on strict disc neighborhoods with singleton Shilov boundary forces constancy by Thuillier2.3.9. Unit-norm rigidity gives the same ordinary-neighborhood conclusion. The normalization has finitely many rigid preimages. Removing the closed image of the compact complement of their constant neighborhoods gives an actual constant ordinary neighborhood downstairs, including nilpotents. Constant sequences σh(a)+4^-n suffice.

At a nonrigid point, remove the locally finite rigid conductor/intersection set. The reduction is one smooth branch. The full semistable disc/annulus/star structure gives an ordinary star inside any prescribed open; compactness requires truncating only finitely many exceptional directions. Choose an actual strict affinoid Y inside it. Its reduced finite skeleton lies in a tree and therefore has no circuit. Harmonic/lisse refinement gives h=F∘τ on one fixed finite tree Γ, with F edgewise affine and zero interior graph Laplacian. The same Y and Γ handle both signs.

For ε>0, root Γ at a boundary vertex. Assign μ=1 to interior vertices, μ=0 to other boundary vertices, and μ(root)=−number of interior vertices. Integer edge slopes given by subtree sums yield Δψ=μ. Add a sufficiently small δψ to σF, then approximate finitely many edge slopes independently by rationals. A tree permits integration without period conditions. With total length L and maximal valency d, the additional uniform error is at most Lη and the Laplacian error at most dη. Thus G is uniformly close and has strictly positive interior vertex masses.

At an interior type-2 vertex z, the rational residual graph divisor B has positive degree. Choose N clearing denominators with deg(NB)≥2g+1. Serre duality gives H¹(O(NB)(−p))=0 for every residual point p. Evaluation is surjective, and over the infinite algebraically closed residue field a section avoids every finitely forbidden graph/exceptional direction. Its effective zero divisor A satisfies A∼NB and has fresh support. Hence B−A/N is a rational multiple of a principal divisor. Thuillier2.3.22’s slope sequences, with residual-function lifting reconstructed using density of the analytic residue field and the annular order formula, give one ordinary unit-log harmonic germ H_z: prescribed graph slopes, fresh slopes −a_p, zero remaining slopes, and value G(z). One finite unit tuple and common lisse refinement provide exact equality on whole ordinary overlaps.

Use the ordinary annular coordinate t=−log|T|+c in each fresh direction. An even smooth mollifier defines m_η(s,t)=(s+t+(|·|*ρ_η)(s−t))/2. This is smooth, convex, nondecreasing, agrees with max outside |s−t|<η, and differs from max by at most η/2. Replace G(z)−at by m_η(G(z)−at,G(z)−ar), choosing η<ar and ar+η/2<ε within a sufficiently short collar. It equals H_z near z and its constant continuation farther down the whole disc. It carries positive curvature and does not return to the old constant. Type-3 positive kinks are smoothed similarly. Finitely many disjoint collars and equality on actual ordinary open overlaps glue a continuous g on Y, ordinary smooth/psh on its interior, with arbitrarily small uniform error. Only scalar tests are partitioned when verifying positivity; psh functions are not glued by partitions.

Nilpotents remain actual. Lift local finite unit tuples through the quotient defining the reduction; their numerical logarithmic norms agree. Scalar-section nullity supplies the same ordinary smooth numerical function on Y. Every actual nonnegative compact ordinary test ψ restricts to a nonnegative reduced test ψ₀, and D commutes with restriction. Uniqueness of the finite extending absolute value makes the embedding isometric on finite K-subfields; completion gives C→F. B’s compatible-root argument proves F algebraically closed. By n1’s reconstructed transport and recognition, locally over C the finite normalization N of the reduction maps surjectively to U_C, is smooth strict boundaryless, and the lifted function is Thuillier harmonic. Base change gives a finite surjective smooth pure-curve cover N_F→U_F. Outside the original locally finite rigid conductor/intersection set it remains an actual isomorphism after reduction. The excluded strict zero-dimensional algebras become finite Artinian F-algebras, so their support remains locally finite and rigid. The original reduction kernel remains nilpotent. Away from that support the actual U_F is a nilpotent thickening of a smooth branch.

Thuillier Proposition2.3.18 preserves the harmonic sheaf on a smooth strict curve under every non-Archimedean extension. Its proof uses Lemma2.3.5: the semistable skeletal scalar map is a surjective G-local isomorphism of weighted integral polyhedra, and boundary support of the graph Laplacian is equivalent before and after extension. Definitions2.3.12–2.3.16 give the sheaf assertion. These complete bodies are embedded in the main manuscript. This transports an already harmonic function, not a current. At excluded rigid points, all finitely many preimages have constant ordinary neighborhoods; finite compact quotient shrinking gives constancy downstairs. At nonrigid points, n1’s ordinary finite-tree/fresh-cap construction and actual nilpotent test argument apply. Bridge H16 therefore gives D[h_F]=0 against every ordinary analytic scalar test. No current equation after F/C was assumed, and Wanner’s test class is not used in reverse.

Geometry is checked separately. Finite surjectivity from N_F makes U_F locally pure one-dimensional: integral finite component images retain their dimensions, and every target minimal component has a source component above it. Scalar affinoid total dimension on U_L is at most one by CLD11.2.3. A point of local dimension zero would have a zero-dimensional affinoid neighborhood after removal of all one-dimensional components. Its scalar extension to F would be nonempty and still zero-dimensional, contradicting purity of U_F. Affinoid presentations, diagonal base change and GR2.11(5′) retain goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness. Actual nilpotents retain their calibration.

Every compact ordinary smooth scalar test ψ on U_L pulls back compactly to U_F: cover its support by finitely many ordinary affinoid interiors and use their compact scalar affinoids. Smooth D commutes with pullback. CLD15.3.1 states that the pushforward of a scalar-pulled locally integrable calibrated (n,n)-form measure equals its original measure. Its embedded proof uses CLD14.3.6 and actual Artinian degree sums, including nilpotents and inseparable degrees. There is no scalar degree factor. Consequently

∫_{U_L}h_L(Dψ)_Rad = ∫_{U_F}h_F(Dπ*ψ)_Rad = 0.

The continuous multiplier is bounded on the compact support. Since ψ was arbitrary, this proves the full ordinary-current equation by measure pairings, not by defining pullback of arbitrary continuous currents.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p063-local-tree-affinoid}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth algebraic $K$-curve, let $W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be
open, and let $x\in W$.  There is a connected strict affinoid domain
$Y\subset W$, with $x\in Y^\circ$, which admits a strictly semistable
skeleton that is a finite metric tree.  Moreover, if $f$ is lisse on a
neighbourhood of $Y$, then, after refining that skeleton and making a
finite metric subdivision, one can write
\[
                         f|_Y=F\circ\tau
\]
for the retraction $\tau:Y\to\Gamma$ onto a finite metric tree $\Gamma$
and a continuous function $F$ that is affine on every edge.  The added
vertices away from the boundary are of type $2$ or type $3$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p063-tree-rational-strictification}
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite metric tree, let $\partial\Gamma$ be a nonempty
set of vertices containing every endpoint designated as boundary, and let
$F:\Gamma\to\mathbf R$ be continuous and affine on every edge.  Suppose
that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-graph-subharmonicity}
 \Delta_\Gamma F(v):=\sum_{e\ni v}d_eF(v)\geq0
 \qquad
 \bigl(v\in V(\Gamma)\setminus\partial\Gamma\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $d_eF(v)$ denotes the outgoing slope.  For every $\varepsilon>0$
there is a continuous function $G:\Gamma\to\mathbf R$, affine with
rational slope on every edge, such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-graph-rational-error}
             \lVert G-F\rVert_{L^\infty(\Gamma)}<\varepsilon
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-graph-strict-mass}
 \Delta_\Gamma G(v)>0
 \qquad
 \bigl(v\in V(\Gamma)\setminus\partial\Gamma\bigr).
\end{equation}
If there are no interior vertices, the last condition is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p063-residual-divisor-moving}
Let $C_0$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g$ over an
infinite algebraically closed field $k_0$, let $M\subset C_0$ be finite, and let
$B\in\operatorname{Div}_{\mathbf Q}(C_0)$ have positive degree.  There are
an integer $N>0$ and an effective integral divisor $A$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-moving-divisor}
          A\sim NB,
          \qquad
          \operatorname{Supp}(A)\cap M=\varnothing.
\end{equation}
Consequently $B-N^{-1}A$ is a rational multiple of a principal divisor.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p063-principal-residual-germ}
Let $K$ be as in \cref{lem:p063-local-tree-affinoid}, let $C$ be a smooth
$K$-analytic curve, and let $v\in C$ be an interior point of type $2$.
Let $C_v$ be its residual smooth projective curve.  Choose finitely many
tangent directions $\xi$ at $v$, let $p_\xi\in C_v(\widetilde K)$ be the
corresponding residual points, and let $r_\xi\in\mathbf Q$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-residual-degree-zero}
                         \sum_\xi r_\xi=0.
\end{equation}
Assume that
\[
                         D=\sum_\xi r_\xi[p_\xi]
\]
is a rational multiple of a principal divisor.  For every $c\in\mathbf R$
there is an ordinary Chambert--Loir--Ducros smooth harmonic germ $h$ at
$v$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-prescribed-residual-slopes}
                    h(v)=c,
                    \qquad
                    d_\xi h(v)=r_\xi
\end{equation}
in the displayed directions and $d_\xi h(v)=0$ in every other tangent
direction.  Here ordinary smoothness means smoothness for analytic moment
maps, not weak smoothness for harmonic tropicalizations.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p063-tree-lisse-ordinary-regularization}
Let $K$ be as above, let $C$ be a smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve, and
let $Y\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be a connected strict affinoid domain
admitting a strictly semistable skeleton that is a finite tree.  Let
$f:Y\to\mathbf R$ be lisse and suppose that $f|_{Y^\circ}$ is
Thuillier-subharmonic.  For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $g\in C(Y)$
such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-lisse-uniform-regularization}
             \lVert g-f\rVert_{L^\infty(Y)}<\varepsilon
\end{equation}
and $g|_{Y^\circ}$ is ordinary Chambert--Loir--Ducros smooth and
plurisubharmonic.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p063-current-psh-ordinary-regularization}
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed, complete, nontrivially valued
non-Archimedean field, let $C$ be a smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve,
and let $W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be open.  For a continuous function
$u:W\to\mathbf R$, the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-current-positivity}
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]\geq0.
\end{equation}
\item The function $u$ is Thuillier-subharmonic.
\item For every $x\in W$, there are a connected strict affinoid domain
$Y\subset W$, with $x\in Y^\circ$, and functions $u_n\in C(Y)$ such that
$u_n|_{Y^\circ}$ is ordinary Chambert--Loir--Ducros smooth and
plurisubharmonic,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p063-monotone-ordinary-approximation}
                         u_{n+1}\leq u_n\quad\text{on }Y,
                         \qquad
                         u_n\longrightarrow u|_Y
\end{equation}
uniformly on $Y$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, in this curve scope, current positivity, Thuillier
subharmonicity, and local membership of a continuous function in the first
ordinary Chambert--Loir--Ducros decreasing-limit stage agree.
\end{theorem}
